name: Patient-AI Rating instrument
description: Importance: Patients increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) for health-related conversations, but evaluation measures largely reflect clinician judgment. Objective: To develop and preliminarily evaluate a patient instrument assessing the quality of patient-AI health conversations. Design: Cross-sectional survey conducted June 5-14, 2026, following patient-partnered instrument development and cognitive interviews. Setting: An anonymous online survey. Participants: A convenience sample of adults with prior use of large language models for personal health-related queries, recruited from an academic medical center-affiliated Insight Panel and patient peers. Exposures: Participants' own prior health-related conversations with AI tools of their choosing. Main Outcomes and Measures: The Patient-AI Rating instrument comprised 12 communication-quality and patient engagement items rated from 1 to 5 and a separately scored patient-perceived-harm item. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach alpha, with sensitivity analyses using first ratings only for those using the tool to rate multiple conversations and participant-mean profiles. We examined item-total correlations, inter-item structure, and between- and within-participant variation. Results: Fourteen participants contributed 46 complete ratings; among 13 providing demographics, median age was 63 years (IQR, 53-70 years), and 8 (62%) reported female gender. Participants provided a median of 2 ratings (range, 1-17).
